labels.name: S7 (Russian airline involved in video production)

podcast.title: First Zero-G Music Video (2014)
podcast.body: OK Go partnered with Russian airline S7 to produce the first-ever Zero-G music video for their song "Upside Down and Inside Out." The video was filmed by flying a plane through a series of extreme parabolic trajectories, creating momentary periods of zero gravity. While Commander Chris Hadfield filmed a Zero-G video in space in 2013, OK Go's video is recognized for being filmed within the Earth's atmosphere. "Ok go teamed with a Russian airline called S7 to create the first ever Zero-G Music video for a song called Upside Down and Inside Out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Contemporary Powerpop
podcast.body: OK Go is recognized as a modern band that carries on the Powerpop legacy, noted for its continued influence on today's artists. Their inclusion signifies the genre's longevity and adaptability through different eras of rock music. "Well we have Jimmy Eat World, OkGo, All American Rejects, Simple Plan, maybe Fallout Boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Self-Promotion and Viral Video Success
podcast.body: OK Go initially achieved significant success through self-promotion, including playing gigs, direct downloads, social media, and creating viral music videos, one of which garnered over 60 million views on YouTube, before eventually signing with a label. "Originally, they were all about self-promotion and made huge strides without signing to a label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Wild Videos as Geek Rock Indicator
podcast.body: Ok Go is considered part of the Geek Rock world primarily because of their elaborate and "wild videos," which are seen as a defining characteristic aligning them with the genre's inventive and often quirky visual approach. "And with all the wild videos they do, you can make a case for Ok Go to be part of the Geek Rock world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Zero-G Video in Space (2013)
xref.body: In 2013, Commander Chris Hadfield produced a Zero-G music video while aboard the International Space Station. This pioneering video preceded OK Go's Zero-G music video, which was filmed within Earth's atmosphere. "And before you point out that Commander Chris Hadfield did a Zero-G video aboard the International Space Station in 2013, you are right."
